sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
ஏனிந்த விளையாடல் அஞ்சனி சுதனே தேவர்
கோன் அடியால் வீங்கிய ஹனுமானே
sections.translit:
Enindha viLaiyAdal anjani suthanE dhEvar
kOn adiyAl vIngiya hanumAnE
sections.en: Oh, Anjanai’s son Hanuman, your cheek swelled after Lord Indra struck you. Why do you play this game?

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
சிவந்த தெல்லாம் பழமென்று எண்ணலாகுமா
உவந்த தென்று நினைந்தே உண்ணலாகுமா
sections.translit:
sivandha dhellAm pazhamendRu eNNalAgumA
uvandha dhendRu ninaindhE uNNalAgumA
sections.en: Is it correct to think that all red circular things are fruits? Is it proper to desire and attempt to eat those?

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
ஆதவன் அனலினை அணைத்தது பின்னால்
மாதவன் துணையாகி (வாலிடை) தீப்பொறி தாங்கவா
சாகா வரம் வாங்கவா கனலிடை கருகாது
வேகா நிலை அடையவா வாயுவோடிழைந்து உறவாடவா
sections.translit:
Adhavan analinai aNaitthadhu pinnAl
mAdhavan thuNaiyAgi (vAlidai) thIppoRi thAngavA
sAgA varam vAngavA kanalidai karugAdhu
vEgA nilai adaiyavA vAyuvOdizhaindhu uRavAdavA
sections.en: Did you have the foresight to get trained in withstanding heat by embracing the sun? Was that a forerunner to carry the sparks on your tail as Rama’s companion? Or was it a pretense to get a boon of longevity? Or was it an attempt to get a boon to be protected by a fire in future? Or was it a plan to spend quality time with the demigod Vayu, your father?

notes: This song was written for Smt. Janani Narayanan of the Nrityakalya Dance Company, Cupertino, CA. It was used as part of her school’s program titled “Bala Hanuman”, performed by the young dancers of her academy. The song is based on a popular episode from Anjaneya’s (the name Anchaneya is also used interchangeably) childhood. One morning, young Anjaneya looked up at the deep red sun in the sky. Mistaking it for a ripe fruit, he began flying toward it. The celestials grew anxious upon witnessing the child’s extraordinary act. Indra, the chief of the demigods, struck him with his powerful weapon. The young lad was hit on the cheek and fell unconscious. Vayu, his father, became enraged and withdrew the flow of air from the universe, terrifying all beings. Indra apologized for his action, and Lord Siva revived Anjaneya. Hanuman received his name because of the elongated cheek that resulted from Indra’s blow. As compensation, Indra granted him strength equal to his own. The other demigods, or devas, blessed him with chiranjivitva or immortality. Brahma blessed him with the ability to change his size at will—expanding or shrinking as needed. Agni granted him immunity from fire, while Varuna blessed him so that no water body could harm him and he could cross any ocean with ease. Vayu bestowed upon him the ability to fly at great speed and spent joyous time with his son, pleased by the blessings offered by the celestials. The Valmiki Ramayana (Kishkindha Kanda, Sarga 66) vividly describes this childhood episode of Anjaneya. Later, when the monkeys were preparing to search for Sita, Anjaneya remained quiet due to a sage’s curse, unaware of his own immense strength. Jambavan, the wise elder bear-warrior, reminded him of his extraordinary abilities—recalling how he once attempted to seize the sun, thinking it was a fruit. For additional details, see the following references: Hanuman: significance of the name ஶ்ரீ ஆஞ்சநேய புராணம், எழுதியவர் கார்த்திகேயன் (எஸ். ராமநாதன்), பதிப்பகத்தார்: கிரி டிரேடிங் ஏஜென்ஸி, 10, கபாலீசுவரர் சன்னதி தெரு, மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை – 4, போன்: 494 0376, இரண்டாம் மறு பதிப்பு: செப்டம்பர் 1999, சிரஞ்சீவி அனுமன், 10 – 12. Puranic support for Anchaneya’s attempt to grab the sun
